Rashi on Sukkah 27b:10:1.hebrew: ששבת בסוכתו של יוחנן כו' - לקמיה פריך: הא אמר ר' אליעזר: ״משבח אני את העצלנין״:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:10:1.english: Who stayed in the sukkah of Yoḥanan, etc. - Later, [the Gemara] challenges: Didn’t Rabbi Eliezer say, “I praise the lazy”?

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:10:2.hebrew: מהו שאפרוש עליה סדין - לצל, שלא תשוזפך השמש — מי אסור משום מוסיף על אהל עראי בשבת, או לא:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:10:2.english: What is [the halakha; may] I spread a sheet over it - For shade, so that the sun will not scorch you: Is it forbidden on account of adding to a temporary tent on Shabbat, or not?

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:10:3.hebrew: אין לך כל שבט כו' - השיאו לדבר אחר, כדאמרי' לקמן (סוכה דף כח.), שלא אמר דבר אחד שלא שמע מפי רבו:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:10:3.english: There is no tribe, etc. - [Rabbi Eliezer] diverted him to another matter, as we say below (Sukkah 28a), that he never said a single thing that he had not heard from his teacher.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:10:4.hebrew: שלא העמיד שופט - מושיע את ישראל, אותן שהיו משמת יהושע ועד שמואל שמשח שאול למלך. יהושע מאפרים, אהוד מבנימין, גדעון ממנשה — הרי מבני רחל. שמשון מדן, ברק מקדש מנפתלי — הרי מבני בלהה. אבצן, זה בועז, מיהודה; עלי מלוי, תולע מיששכר, אלון הזבולני מזבולן — אלו מפורשים. אבל עתניאל, ויפתח, ושמגר, ויאיר, ועבדון — לא ידעתי שמות שבטיהן; ומראובן ושמעון, גד ואשר — לא מצאתי מפורש:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:10:4.english: That did not produce a judge - [Meaning,] a deliverer of Israel; [namely,] those who were [judges] from the death of Joshua until Samuel, who anointed Saul as king. Joshua was from Ephraim, Ehud from Benjamin, [and] Gideon from Manasseh — behold, [these are] from the descendants of Rachel. Samson was from Dan, [and] Barak of Kedesh from Naphtali — behold, [these are] from the descendants of Bilhah. Ibzan — this is Boaz — was from Judah; Eli from Levi; Tola from Issachar; Elon the Zebulunite from Zebulun — these are explicitly stated [in Scripture]. But [as for] Othniel, Jephthah, Shamgar, Jair, and Abdon — I do not know the names of their tribes; and from Reuben, Simeon, Gad, and Asher, I have not found [a judge] explicitly stated.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:11:1.english: The sun reached - [The sun was] spreading and drawing near to them.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:11:2.hebrew: מלכים על פי נביאים - שאול ודוד ע"פ שמואל:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:11:2.english: Kings according to prophets - Saul and David [were established] by the word of Samuel.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:11:3.english: And he went out - Because he did not want to permit the matter.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:11:4.hebrew: לא מפני שהפליגו בדברים - מה שהשיאו לדבר אחר, לא הפליגו הימנו ולדחותו שלא ללמדו תורה נתכוון, אלא שלא אמר דבר כו':
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:11:4.english: Not because he diverted him with words - That which he diverted him to another matter, he did not intend to dismiss him from himself and rebuff him so as not to teach him Torah, but rather because he never said a matter, etc.:

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:12:1.hebrew: אין יוצאין מסוכה לסוכה כו' - והאיך הניח שבת שבתוך הרגל את סוכתו שהיתה בלוד? שהיה דר בלוד, כדתניא (סנהדרין ד' לב:): ״אחר ר' אליעזר ללוד״:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:12:1.english: One may not depart from [one] sukkah to [another] sukkah, etc. - And how could he have left, [on] the Shabbat that is within the Festival, his sukkah that was in Lod? For he resided in Lod, as it is taught [in a baraita] (Sanhedrin 32b): “[Follow] after Rabbi Eliezer to Lod.”

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:12:2.hebrew: רגל אחר היה - כגון עצרת, והיו יושבין בסוכה משום אויר:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:12:2.english: It was another Festival - Such as Atzeret [Shavuot], and they were sitting in the sukkah for [fresh] air.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:14:1.hebrew: ותפשוט ליה מדידיה - שלא תפרוש עליה סדין, דאסור להוסיף על אהל עראי:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:14:1.english: And let him resolve it from his own [teaching] - That one may not spread a sheet over it, for it is forbidden to add to a temporary tent.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:14:2.english: That is tied and hanging - [It is] there at all times.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:14:3.hebrew: פוקקין בו - כיון דמתוקן ועומד לכך, אין זה לא בונה ולא מוסיף:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:14:3.english: One may shutter with it - Since it is prepared and stands designated for this, this is neither building nor adding [to a tent].

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:14:4.english: And if not, one may not shutter with it - For he is adding to the closure of a tent.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:1:1.hebrew: אין יוצאין מסוכה לסוכה - לאכול בזו ולישן בזו, או היום בזו ומחר בזו:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:1:1.english: One may not depart from [one] sukkah to [another] sukkah - To eat in this [one] and sleep in that [one], or today in this [one] and tomorrow in that [one].

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:1:2.hebrew: ואין עושין סוכה בחולו של מועד - מי שלא ישב בסוכה י"ט הראשון:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:1:2.english: And one may not make a sukkah during the intermediate days of the Festival - [This refers to] one who did not sit in a sukkah on the first day of the Festival.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:2:1.hebrew: עשה סוכה לשם חג של שבעת הימים - שמעת מינה דאין עושין סוכה בחולו של מועד, דאינה לשבעה; ושמעינן מינה דאין יוצאין מסוכה לסוכה, דאם כן, לאו סוכה לשבעה היא:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:2:1.english: Make a sukka for the sake of the festival of seven days - You deduce from it that one does not make a sukka on the intermediate days of the Festival [Chol HaMoed], as it is not for seven [days]; and we deduce from it that one does not go from sukka to sukka, for if so, it is not a sukka for seven [days].

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:3:1.english: [It is] obvious - For behold, it is a sukkah of seven [days].

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:3:2.hebrew: מהו דתימא האי אחריתי היא ואינה לשבעה קמ"ל - הואיל וישב בה בי"ט, וזו להשלים היא — סוכת שבעה קרינא ביה, שתשלומין לראשונה היא:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:3:2.english: Lest you say this is a different one and is not for seven [days], it teaches us - Since he sat in it on the Festival day, and this [one] is to complete [it], we can read concerning it 'a sukkah of seven [days],' as it is a completion of the first [one].

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:4:1.english: “For yourselves” — from your own - To exclude that which is stolen and that which is borrowed.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:5:1.hebrew: כל האזרח ישבו בסוכות כתיב - דמשמע סוכה אחת לכל ישראל, שישבו בה זה אחר זה. ואי אפשר שיהא לכולן, דלא מטי שוה פרוטה לכל חד, אלא ע"י שאלה:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:5:1.english: "All the homeborn shall reside in sukkot" is written - Which implies one sukka for all of Israel, in which they will reside one after another. And it is impossible that [the sukka] could belong to all of them, as [a share] worth a peruta does not reach each one; rather, [it can only be] through borrowing.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:7:1.english: In the interim - During the intermediate days of the Festival.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:7:2.hebrew: וקטן שנתגדל - צמחו לו ב' שערות במועד, ואתא האי כל לרבויי שעושה סוכה בחולו של מועד, מה שאין כן במחויב קודם לכן, כדאמר ר' אליעזר לעיל:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:7:2.english: And a minor who reached majority - Two [pubic] hairs grew on him during the Festival, and this [word] “all” comes to include [him, teaching] that he makes a sukka on the intermediate days of the Festival, which is not the case for one who was obligated prior to this, as Rabbi Eliezer stated above.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:7:3.hebrew: ורבנן כיון דאמרי עושין סוכה בחולו של מועד - ואפי' מי שמחויב קודם לכן ולא עשה, תו לא איצטריך האי לרבויי, דכ"ש הוא:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:7:3.english: And the Rabbis, since they say one may make a sukka on the intermediate days of the Festival - and even someone who was obligated prior to this and did not make [one may do so] — this [verse] was no longer needed to include [them], for it is an a fortiori [argument].

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:8:1.hebrew: ברגל - י"ט ראשון, והלך אצלו מערב י"ט:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:8:1.english: On the Festival - [On the] first day of the Festival, and he had gone to him on the eve of the Festival.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:8:2.english: You are not among those who rest on the Festival - Since you did not stay in your home with your wife.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:8:3.hebrew: משבח אני את העצלנין - אע"פ שלא בשביל הרגל מתעכבים — שהרי כל ימות השנה אינן יוצאין מחמת עצלות — אעפ"כ משבחן אני:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:8:3.english: I praise the lazy - Even though they do not stay [home] on account of the Festival — for all days of the year they do not go out due to laziness — nevertheless, I praise them.

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:9:1.hebrew: מדוע את הולכת וגו' - בעלה של שונמית אמר לה, כשאמרה לו: ״אלכה וארוצה עד איש האלהים ואשובה״:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:9:1.english: “Why are you going,” etc. - The husband of the Shunammite [woman] said [this] to her when she said to him: “Let me go and run to the man of God and return.”

Rashi on Sukkah 27b:9:2.hebrew: הא דאזיל ואתי ביומיה - ומשמח שמחת החג עם אשתו, חייב להקביל פני רבו — כגון עיר שבתוך התחום, או על ידי עירוב:
Rashi on Sukkah 27b:9:2.english: This [is a case] where he goes and returns on the same day - and [thus also] rejoices in the joy of the Festival with his wife, [in which case] he is obligated to greet his teacher; such as [visiting] a town that is within the [Shabbat] boundary, or by means of an eruv.

Tosafot on Sukkah 27b:14:1.hebrew: פקק החלון - פירשנו לעיל בפרק קמא (סוכה דף טז:), גבי "שכחו ולא הביאו ספר תורה":
Tosafot on Sukkah 27b:14:1.english: A window shutter - We explained [this] above in the first chapter (Sukkah 16b), regarding [the case of]: "They forgot and did not bring a Torah scroll."

Tosafot on Sukkah 27b:3:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא כיון דנפלה אחריתי היא - יש ספרים שכתוב בהן: "קמ"ל, כיון (דבדידי') קעביד — איהי היא". משמע: לפי שבונה אותה באותן עצים:
Tosafot on Sukkah 27b:3:1.english: "Lest you say: Since it collapsed, it is a different one" - There are books in which it is written: "It teaches us: Since he makes [it] (with its own [materials]), it is [the very same] one." This implies: because he rebuilds it with those [same] pieces of wood.

Tosafot on Sukkah 27b:5:1.hebrew: כל האזרח בישראל ישבו בסוכות - משמע סוכה אחת לכל ישראל, שישבו בה זה אחר זה; ואי אפשר שתהא של כולם, דלא מטי שוה פרוטה לכל אחד, אלא על ידי שאלה. כך פירש בקונט'. ועל חנם דחק; דכיון דכתב "לך", למעוטי דשותפין משמע, כדמוכח בראשית הגז (חולין דף קלו.) גבי תרומה וחלה ופאה, וטובא דקא חשיב התם. ואפי' אתרוג נמי, דכתיב ביה "לכם" לשון רבים, אמרינן ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קלז:): האחין שקנו אתרוג בתפיסת הבית, ונוטלו אחד מהם ויוצא בו, אם יכול לאכלו — כגון דאיכא אתרוג כיוצא בו לכל חד וחד — יצא, ואם לאו — לא יצא; ד"לכם" משמע שיהא כולו שלו ולא מקצתו, ולא דמי לבגדיכם ועריסותיכם ותרומותיכם דפרק ראשית הגז (חולין דף קלו.), דשל שותפין בכלל. והא דכתיב "לכם" לשון רבים — משום דאיבעי ליה למיכתב "ולקחתם" לשון רבים, דדרשינן פרק לולב וערבה (לקמן סוכה דף מג.) שתהא לקיחה לכל אחד ואחד. (ומרבינן) סוכה אחת לכל ישראל — שמע מינה דלא דרשי "לך" למעוטי שאולה, ומוקמי ליה למעוטי גזולה. ומיהו קשה: הא גבי ציצית מרבינן דשותפין מדכתיב "בגדיהם", וממעטינן שאולה מדכתיב "כסותך" בפ' ראשית הגז (חולין דף קלו.); וא"כ, הכא נמי נידרוש הכי! ולפירוש הקונטרס ניחא, דעל כרחך יוצאין בשאולה, מדמרבינן סוכה אחת לכל ישראל. ותימה: דלר' אליעזר דבעי "סוכה שלכם", אין שנים יוצאין בסוכה א' לעולם, ויהא צריך לכל בני הבית סוכה לכל אחד וא'? ושמא הוה מרבי מדכתיב "תשבו כעין תדורו" (שותפין), שיכולים לישב יחד בסוכה אחת. ומה שנהגו כל הקהל לקנות אתרוג בשותפות לצאת בו — דעתן להקנות כל א' חלקו לחבירו בשעה שהוא מברך על מנת להחזיר; דבשביל שנשתתף בו לא גרע ממתנה על מנת להחזיר, דשמה מתנה:
Tosafot on Sukkah 27b:5:1.english: "All the homeborn in Israel shall reside in sukkot" - This implies [there may be] one sukkah for all of Israel, in which they reside one after another. And it is impossible that it belongs to all of them, for a perutah's value would not reach each one; rather, [they fulfill their obligation] by means of borrowing. So it was explained in the Kuntres [Rashi]. And he struggled needlessly, for since [the Torah] writes "to you" [lekha, in the singular], it implies the exclusion of [property belonging to] partners, as is demonstrated in [the chapter] Reishit HaGez (Chullin 136a) regarding terumah, challah, and pe'ah, and the many [mitzvot] that [the Gemara] enumerates there. And even with regard to an etrog, concerning which "to you" [lakhem] is written in the plural, we say in [the chapter] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 137b): [In the case of] brothers who purchased an etrog from the undivided estate, and one of them takes it and fulfills [his obligation] with it, if he can eat it — such as where there is a corresponding etrog for each and every one — he has fulfilled [his obligation]; but if not, he has not fulfilled [his obligation], because "to you" implies that it must be entirely his and not [merely] part of it. And it is not similar to "your garments" [bigdeikhem], "your doughs" [arisoteikhem], and "your gifts" [terumoteikhem] in the chapter Reishit HaGez (Chullin 136a), where that of partners is included. And as for that which is written "to you" [lakhem] in the plural, [this is] because it needed to write "and you shall take" [ul’kakhtem] in the plural, as we expound in the chapter Lulav Ve’Aravah (below, Sukkah 43a): that there must be a taking by each and every individual. And [since] we include one sukkah for all of Israel, learn from it that they do not expound "to you" [lekha] to exclude a borrowed [sukkah], but rather establish it to exclude a stolen [one]. However, this is difficult: For regarding tzitzit, we include [a garment belonging to] partners because it is written "their garments" [vigdeihem], and we exclude a borrowed [garment] because it is written "your garment" [kesutekha], in the chapter Reishit HaGez (Chullin 136a); and if so, here too let us expound likewise! And according to the explanation of the Kuntres, it is well, for perforce one fulfills [his obligation] with a borrowed [sukkah], since we include one sukkah for all of Israel. And it is astonishing: according to Rabbi Eliezer, who requires a sukkah "of your own," can two people never fulfill [their obligation] in one sukkah, and each member of the household would require a sukkah for each and every one?! And perhaps he would include [partners] from that which is written: "You shall reside" — in the manner that you dwell, [such that partners] can reside together in one sukkah. And as for that which the entire congregation is accustomed to purchase an etrog in partnership to fulfill [their obligation] with it — their intention is for each one to transfer ownership of his share to his fellow at the time that he recites the blessing, on condition that he return it; for because he is a partner in it, it is no worse than a gift given on condition that it be returned, which is deemed a valid gift.
